description: Design a voice agent from use case definition through conversation flow mapping to handoff planning.

steps.description: Define the use cases and user personas for a voice agent.

inputs.name: business-context
inputs.desc: Description of the business and its customers

inputs.name: target-interactions
inputs.desc: Types of interactions the voice agent should handle

outputs.name: use-case-catalog
outputs.desc: List of use cases with priority, volume estimate, and complexity rating

outputs.name: user-personas
outputs.desc: Personas describing the target callers and their goals

process: Inventory the interactions the voice agent should handle, ranked by volume and value.
Define user personas with their goals, technical comfort, and common frustrations.
Rate each use case by complexity (simple lookup, multi-turn, requires authentication).
Select the use cases for the initial launch versus later phases.

steps.description: Map the conversation flows for each use case, including intents, entities, and dialog turns.

outputs.name: conversation-flows
outputs.desc: Dialog flow diagrams for each use case with intents, entities, and branching logic

outputs.name: intent-entity-schema
outputs.desc: Catalog of intents and entities with example utterances

process: For each use case, map the happy path dialog from greeting to resolution.
Identify the intents (what the user wants) and entities (the data they provide) at each turn.
Add branching paths for ambiguous input, missing information, and confirmation steps.
Write 5 to 10 example utterances per intent to cover phrasing variation.

steps.description: Write the voice prompts and response templates for each dialog turn.

outputs.name: prompt-templates
outputs.desc: Written prompts for every dialog turn, including confirmations and clarifications

outputs.name: response-library
outputs.desc: Library of response variants to avoid repetition

process: Write the initial greeting and identity verification prompts.
Write the prompts for each dialog turn, keeping them short and natural.
Create response variants (at least 3 per prompt) to avoid sounding robotic.
Write the closing and post-interaction summary prompts.

steps.description: Design the fallback and error handling paths for unrecognized input and system failures.

outputs.name: fallback-flows
outputs.desc: Fallback paths for unrecognized input, repeated failures, and system errors

outputs.name: escalation-triggers
outputs.desc: Conditions that trigger handoff to a human agent

process: Define the fallback response for unrecognized input (reprompt, rephrase, offer options).
Set the escalation threshold (e.g., after 2 failed recognition attempts, hand off).
Design the system error handling (API timeout, service unavailable).
Write the handoff prompt that transfers context to the human agent.

steps.description: Test the voice agent with sample conversations and measure recognition accuracy.

outputs.name: test-results
outputs.desc: Results from sample conversation tests including intent accuracy and task completion rate

outputs.name: voice-agent-design-doc
outputs.desc: Final voice agent design document combining all flows, prompts, and test results

process: Run each use case through the happy path with sample utterances.
Run edge cases: ambiguous input, out-of-scope requests, silence, interruptions.
Measure intent recognition accuracy and task completion rate.
Compile the design document with flows, prompts, fallbacks, and test results.

description: Design an IVR phone menu system from caller journey mapping through prompt writing to call path testing.

steps.description: Map the caller journey from entry to resolution for each call type.

inputs.name: call-types
inputs.desc: List of call types the IVR should handle (billing, support, sales, etc.)

inputs.name: call-volume-data
inputs.desc: Volume and distribution of calls by type

outputs.name: caller-journeys
outputs.desc: Journey maps for each call type from dial-in to resolution

outputs.name: routing-requirements
outputs.desc: Where each call type should land (queue, agent group, self-service)

process: List the call types and their percentage of total volume.
Map each call type from the moment the caller dials in to resolution or transfer.
Identify which calls can be fully self-served versus those requiring an agent.
Document the routing destination for each call type.

steps.description: Define the IVR menu tree with options, routing, and shortcuts.

inputs.name: caller-journeys
inputs.desc: Journey maps for each call type

outputs.name: menu-tree
outputs.desc: Complete IVR menu tree with numbered options, sub-menus, and routing targets

outputs.name: shortcut-map
outputs.desc: DTMF shortcuts for frequent callers (e.g., press 0 for agent)

process: Design the top-level menu with no more than 5 options, ordered by call volume.
Add sub-menus only where necessary, keeping the tree no deeper than 3 levels.
Define shortcuts: press 0 for agent, press # to repeat, press * for main menu.
Map each terminal menu option to its routing destination.

steps.description: Write the voice prompts for each menu level and option.

outputs.name: ivr-prompts
outputs.desc: Written prompts for every menu, including greeting, options, and error messages

outputs.name: ivr-prompt-timing
outputs.desc: Estimated duration of each prompt in seconds

process: Write the welcome greeting (company name, brief instruction, language selection if needed).
Write each menu prompt: state the options clearly with the number first ('Press 1 for...').
Write the error prompts: invalid input, timeout, and maximum retries exceeded.
Time each prompt to keep menu levels under 30 seconds total.

steps.description: Configure the DTMF inputs, speech recognition, and call routing rules.

outputs.name: routing-config
outputs.desc: Routing rules mapping each input to a destination (queue, agent group, self-service module)

outputs.name: recognition-config
outputs.desc: DTMF and speech recognition settings for each menu level

process: Map each DTMF keypress to its routing destination.
Configure speech recognition grammars if the system supports spoken input.
Set timeout durations (how long to wait for input before reprompting).
Define the maximum retry count before routing to a default agent queue.

steps.description: Test all IVR call paths and produce the IVR design document.

outputs.name: call-path-test-results
outputs.desc: Results of testing each path through the IVR, noting any dead ends or loops

outputs.name: ivr-design-document
outputs.desc: Complete IVR design document with menu tree, prompts, routing, and test results

process: Walk each call path from entry to resolution, testing every menu option.
Verify that no path leads to a dead end or infinite loop.
Test the error paths: invalid input, timeout, and maximum retries.
Compile the IVR design document with the menu tree, prompts, routing config, and test results.

description: Set up call center operations from service level definition through routing and quality monitoring.

steps.description: Define the service levels for call center operations.

inputs.name: business-requirements
inputs.desc: Customer service goals and SLA commitments

inputs.name: call-volume-forecast
inputs.desc: Expected call volumes by hour and day

outputs.name: service-level-targets
outputs.desc: Targets for answer time, abandon rate, handle time, and first-call resolution

outputs.name: staffing-model
outputs.desc: Staffing requirements by hour to meet service level targets

process: Set the target answer speed (e.g., 80% of calls answered within 20 seconds).
Set the maximum abandon rate, average handle time target, and first-call resolution target.
Model the staffing requirement using the call volume forecast and service level targets.
Document the service level agreement for internal and external use.

steps.description: Design the call routing logic including skills-based routing and queue priority.

outputs.name: routing-logic
outputs.desc: Call routing rules: skills-based assignment, queue priority, overflow rules

outputs.name: queue-config
outputs.desc: Queue definitions with priority levels and overflow thresholds

process: Define agent skill groups (billing, technical, sales, general).
Set the routing priority: match caller need to agent skill, then least-idle agent.
Design the overflow rules for when a queue exceeds its wait time threshold.
Configure VIP or priority routing for high-value customers.

steps.description: Build the agent scripts for common call types.

outputs.name: agent-scripts
outputs.desc: Scripts for each call type: opening, verification, troubleshooting, closing

outputs.name: knowledge-base-links
outputs.desc: Links to relevant knowledge base articles for each call type

process: Write the standard opening (greeting, identification, verification).
Write the resolution scripts for each common call type.
Write the escalation script for when the agent cannot resolve the issue.
Write the closing script (summary, next steps, satisfaction check).

steps.description: Set up the quality monitoring program for call center agents.

inputs.name: agent-scripts
inputs.desc: Agent scripts for each call type

outputs.name: quality-scorecard
outputs.desc: Scorecard for evaluating call quality (greeting, resolution, compliance, tone)

outputs.name: monitoring-schedule
outputs.desc: Schedule for call monitoring: sample size, frequency, evaluator assignments

process: Define the quality scorecard dimensions: greeting, verification, resolution accuracy, compliance, tone.
Set the scoring scale and passing threshold.
Determine the sample size (calls per agent per month) and selection method.
Assign evaluators and set the calibration schedule.

steps.description: Build the real-time and historical reporting dashboard for call center operations.

outputs.name: dashboard-spec
outputs.desc: Dashboard layout with real-time metrics (calls in queue, wait time, agents available) and historical trends

outputs.name: call-center-operations-plan
outputs.desc: Complete call center operations plan covering service levels, routing, scripts, quality, and reporting

process: Define the real-time wallboard metrics: calls in queue, longest wait, agents available, service level.
Define the historical report metrics: handle time trend, abandon rate, first-call resolution, quality scores.
Set the alert thresholds for real-time metrics (e.g., queue exceeds 10 calls).
Compile the operations plan document.

description: Build a speech-to-text pipeline from engine selection through post-processing and accuracy validation.

steps.description: Select the speech-to-text engine based on language, accuracy, and latency requirements.

inputs.name: stt-requirements
inputs.desc: Requirements: languages, accuracy target, latency budget, volume, cost constraints

inputs.name: audio-characteristics
inputs.desc: Source audio properties: sample rate, codec, noise level, speaker count

outputs.name: engine-selection
outputs.desc: Selected STT engine with rationale (e.g., Whisper, Google STT, Azure, Deepgram)

outputs.name: engine-config
outputs.desc: Configuration parameters for the selected engine

process: List candidate engines and compare on language support, accuracy benchmarks, and pricing.
Test each candidate against a sample of the target audio.
Select the engine that meets the accuracy target within the latency and cost budget.
Document the configuration parameters (model size, language code, punctuation settings).

steps.description: Configure the audio preprocessing pipeline for noise reduction and normalization.

outputs.name: preprocessing-pipeline
outputs.desc: Audio preprocessing steps: noise reduction, normalization, resampling, channel selection

outputs.name: preprocessing-config
outputs.desc: Configuration for each preprocessing step

process: Set the target sample rate and format for the STT engine.
Configure noise reduction (spectral gating, noise floor threshold).
Set volume normalization to a consistent level.
Handle multi-channel audio (select channel or mix down).

steps.description: Apply post-processing to the raw transcription output.

outputs.name: post-processing-rules
outputs.desc: Rules for punctuation restoration, speaker diarization, and text formatting

outputs.name: output-schema
outputs.desc: Schema for the final transcript output (timestamps, speaker labels, confidence scores)

process: Configure punctuation and capitalization restoration.
Set up speaker diarization (identify and label each speaker).
Define the output format: plain text, timestamped segments, or structured JSON.
Add domain-specific vocabulary corrections (proper nouns, technical terms).

steps.description: Validate transcription accuracy against reference transcripts and produce the pipeline documentation.

outputs.name: accuracy-report
outputs.desc: Word error rate and accuracy metrics against reference transcripts

outputs.name: stt-pipeline-doc
outputs.desc: Complete pipeline documentation covering engine selection, preprocessing, post-processing, and accuracy results

process: Prepare a reference transcript set (manually verified ground truth).
Run the pipeline on the reference audio and compare output to ground truth.
Calculate word error rate (WER) and segment-level accuracy.
Compile the pipeline documentation with configuration, accuracy results, and known limitations.

description: Set up text-to-speech from engine and voice selection through SSML configuration and quality testing.

steps.description: Select the TTS engine and voice based on language, style, and naturalness requirements.

inputs.name: tts-requirements
inputs.desc: Requirements: languages, voice style (warm, professional, casual), use case (IVR, narration, assistant)

inputs.name: brand-voice-guidelines
inputs.desc: Brand voice and tone guidelines if available

outputs.name: tts-engine-selection
outputs.desc: Selected TTS engine and voice with rationale

outputs.name: voice-samples
outputs.desc: Sample audio from the selected voice for stakeholder review

process: List candidate TTS engines and their available voices.
Filter by language support and voice style match.
Generate sample audio for each finalist voice using representative phrases.
Select the voice that best matches the brand tone and naturalness requirements.

steps.description: Configure the speech parameters and SSML markup for pauses, emphasis, and prosody.

inputs.name: voice-samples
inputs.desc: Sample audio from the selected voice

outputs.name: speech-parameters
outputs.desc: Configured rate, pitch, and volume settings

outputs.name: ssml-templates
outputs.desc: SSML templates for common patterns (pauses, emphasis, lists, numbers, dates)

process: Set the speaking rate, pitch, and volume for the target use case.
Write SSML templates for pauses between sentences and list items.
Write SSML templates for emphasis on key words and proper noun pronunciation.
Write SSML templates for reading numbers, dates, currency, and phone numbers correctly.

steps.description: Test TTS output quality and set up the production endpoint.

outputs.name: tts-test-results
outputs.desc: Quality test results across target phrases, including naturalness ratings and pronunciation errors

outputs.name: tts-setup-document
outputs.desc: Complete TTS setup document with engine, voice, parameters, SSML templates, and test results

process: Generate audio for a test set covering all SSML patterns and edge cases.
Review each sample for naturalness, pronunciation accuracy, and pacing.
Fix any pronunciation errors using phoneme overrides or lexicon entries.
Document the production endpoint configuration and compile the setup document.

description: Design conversational UX from persona definition through dialog scripting and user testing.

steps.description: Define the persona and tone of voice for the conversational agent.

inputs.name: target-audience
inputs.desc: Description of the users who will interact with the agent

outputs.name: bot-persona
outputs.desc: Persona document: name, personality traits, tone, vocabulary, things it says and does not say

outputs.name: tone-examples
outputs.desc: Example responses showing the persona in different contexts (greeting, error, success, empathy)

process: Define the persona's personality traits (helpful, direct, warm, professional).
Set the vocabulary level and formality for the target audience.
Write examples of what the persona says and does not say.
Create tone examples for different emotional contexts (neutral, frustrated user, success).

steps.description: Map the user intents and design the dialog flows for each conversation type.

outputs.name: dialog-flows
outputs.desc: Dialog flow diagrams for each conversation type with branching logic

outputs.name: intent-map
outputs.desc: Map of user intents to dialog flows with example utterances

process: List the conversation types the agent will handle.
For each type, map the dialog from trigger to resolution including branches.
Define the intents and slot-filling requirements at each turn.
Identify the decision points where the flow branches based on user input.

steps.description: Write the conversation scripts for greetings, confirmations, errors, and closings.

outputs.name: conversation-scripts
outputs.desc: Scripts for all dialog turns including greetings, confirmations, disambiguation, errors, and closings

outputs.name: multimodal-elements
outputs.desc: Design for buttons, cards, quick replies, and carousels where applicable

process: Write the greeting and disambiguation scripts in the persona's voice.
Write confirmation and error scripts (typo correction, ambiguity resolution, out-of-scope).
Design the multimodal elements (quick reply buttons, cards) for chat interfaces.
Write the closing scripts with next-step suggestions.

steps.description: Test the conversational UX with user walkthroughs and produce the design document.

outputs.name: ux-test-results
outputs.desc: Results from user walkthrough testing including task completion, confusion points, and satisfaction

outputs.name: conversational-ux-design-doc
outputs.desc: Complete conversational UX design document

process: Run user walkthroughs for each conversation type with representative users.
Note confusion points, abandoned conversations, and unexpected user inputs.
Measure task completion rate and user satisfaction.
Compile the design document with persona, flows, scripts, multimodal elements, and test results.

description: Test a voice or chat bot from test scenario definition through automated and human evaluation.

steps.description: Define the test scenarios for a voice or chat bot.

inputs.name: bot-design-doc
inputs.desc: The bot's design document with intents, flows, and prompts

inputs.name: known-issues
inputs.desc: Any known issues or edge cases from prior testing

outputs.name: test-scenarios
outputs.desc: Test scenarios covering happy path, edge cases, and failure modes for each intent

outputs.name: test-utterances
outputs.desc: Test utterances for each scenario with expected intent and entity matches

process: Write happy path scenarios for every intent.
Write edge case scenarios: typos, slang, multi-intent utterances, out-of-scope requests.
Write failure mode scenarios: system errors, timeout, repeated misrecognition.
Compile 10 to 20 test utterances per intent covering phrasing variation.

steps.description: Run automated intent recognition and dialog completion tests.

outputs.name: automated-test-results
outputs.desc: Intent recognition accuracy, entity extraction accuracy, and dialog completion rates

outputs.name: confusion-matrix
outputs.desc: Confusion matrix showing which intents are misclassified and to what

process: Run each test utterance through the bot and record the matched intent and extracted entities.
Compare against expected values and calculate intent accuracy and entity extraction accuracy.
Generate the confusion matrix to identify systematic misclassifications.
Flag intents with accuracy below the threshold for retraining.

steps.description: Conduct human evaluation of response quality and naturalness.

outputs.name: human-eval-results
outputs.desc: Human ratings for response relevance, naturalness, helpfulness, and tone

outputs.name: bot-testing-report
outputs.desc: Complete testing report with automated metrics, human evaluation, and recommendations

process: Select a sample of conversations (mix of successful and failed) for human review.
Rate each response on relevance, naturalness, helpfulness, and tone consistency.
Identify the responses that need rewriting or flow changes.
Compile the testing report with automated metrics, human ratings, and prioritized fixes.

description: Transcribe and summarize meetings from recording through speaker identification to action item extraction.

steps.description: Prepare the meeting audio for transcription.

inputs.name: meeting-recording
inputs.desc: Audio or video file of the meeting

inputs.name: participant-list
inputs.desc: List of meeting participants for speaker identification

outputs.name: prepared-audio
outputs.desc: Audio file preprocessed for transcription (noise reduced, normalized, correct format)

outputs.name: speaker-profiles
outputs.desc: Speaker profiles for diarization (name, voice sample if available)

process: Extract audio from video if needed and convert to the target format.
Apply noise reduction and volume normalization.
Map participant names to speaker profiles for diarization.
Segment the audio if the meeting exceeds the engine's maximum duration.

steps.description: Transcribe the meeting audio with speaker identification.

outputs.name: raw-transcript
outputs.desc: Timestamped transcript with speaker labels

outputs.name: transcription-confidence
outputs.desc: Confidence scores and flagged low-confidence segments

process: Run the transcription engine with speaker diarization enabled.
Label each segment with the identified speaker.
Flag segments with low confidence for manual review.
Merge segments from the same speaker that were split by short pauses.

steps.description: Generate the meeting summary with decisions, action items, and key discussion points.

outputs.name: meeting-summary
outputs.desc: Summary: agenda topics covered, key decisions, action items with owners and deadlines

outputs.name: meeting-record
outputs.desc: Complete meeting record (full transcript, summary, action items, attendance)

process: Extract the agenda topics discussed and summarize each one.
Identify decisions made and who made them.
Extract action items with assigned owner and deadline.
Compile the meeting record with full transcript, summary, and action items.

description: Set up voice analytics from metric definition through pipeline configuration and dashboard creation.

steps.description: Define the voice analytics metrics to track.

inputs.name: analytics-goals
inputs.desc: What the organization wants to learn from voice data (quality, compliance, sentiment, efficiency)

inputs.name: data-sources
inputs.desc: Available voice data sources (call recordings, voicebot logs, IVR logs)

outputs.name: metrics-catalog
outputs.desc: Catalog of metrics: call duration, sentiment score, silence ratio, talk-over rate, compliance phrases, resolution indicator

outputs.name: data-requirements
outputs.desc: Data requirements for each metric (audio features, transcript fields, metadata)

process: List the analytics goals and map each to one or more measurable metrics.
Define each metric: what it measures, how it is calculated, and what data it needs.
Set the baseline and target for each metric.
Identify the data sources and confirm availability.

steps.description: Configure the audio analysis pipeline for the defined metrics.

outputs.name: analysis-pipeline
outputs.desc: Configured pipeline: audio ingestion, feature extraction, metric calculation, storage

outputs.name: alert-rules
outputs.desc: Alert rules for anomalous calls (high silence, negative sentiment, compliance violation)

process: Design the pipeline stages: ingest, transcribe, extract features, calculate metrics, store.
Configure the feature extraction for each metric (sentiment model, silence detector, talk-over detector).
Set the alert thresholds for each metric.
Define the data retention policy for audio and analytics results.

steps.description: Build the voice analytics dashboard and produce the setup document.

outputs.name: analytics-dashboard
outputs.desc: Dashboard layout with metric trends, agent comparisons, and alert feed

outputs.name: voice-analytics-setup-doc
outputs.desc: Complete voice analytics setup document covering metrics, pipeline, alerts, and dashboard

process: Design the dashboard with metric trend charts, agent-level comparisons, and a recent alerts feed.
Set the refresh frequency and data aggregation periods (hourly, daily, weekly).
Configure drill-down from dashboard metrics to individual call recordings.
Compile the setup document with metrics, pipeline config, alert rules, and dashboard spec.

description: Localize a conversational bot for multiple languages from inventory through translation and testing.

steps.description: Inventory the supported languages and plan the localization scope.

inputs.name: target-languages
inputs.desc: Languages and locales the bot should support

inputs.name: bot-content-inventory
inputs.desc: Inventory of all user-facing strings, prompts, and dialog flows

outputs.name: localization-plan
outputs.desc: Plan: languages, priority order, content to translate, cultural adaptation notes

outputs.name: string-catalog
outputs.desc: Extracted string catalog with keys, source text, and context notes for translators

process: List the target languages and locales, ordered by user base size.
Extract all user-facing strings from the bot's prompts, responses, buttons, and error messages.
Tag each string with context (where it appears, what it refers to) for translator reference.
Note cultural adaptations needed beyond translation (date formats, currency, naming conventions).

steps.description: Translate and culturally adapt the bot content for each target language.

inputs.name: localization-plan
inputs.desc: Localization plan with cultural adaptation notes

outputs.name: translated-content
outputs.desc: Translated strings for each target language with cultural adaptations applied

outputs.name: translation-review-notes
outputs.desc: Reviewer notes on translations that need native speaker verification

process: Translate each string maintaining the original tone and intent.
Adapt culturally specific references (idioms, examples, humor, formality levels).
Adjust for text expansion or contraction (some languages are 30% longer than English).
Flag translations that need native speaker review.

steps.description: Configure language detection and routing for the multilingual bot.

outputs.name: language-routing-config
outputs.desc: Configuration for automatic language detection and routing to the correct language model

outputs.name: fallback-language-rules
outputs.desc: Rules for when language detection is uncertain or the language is unsupported

process: Configure automatic language detection from the user's first message.
Set up routing to the correct language-specific dialog and response set.
Define fallback behavior: ask the user to choose a language, or default to the primary language.
Handle code-switching (user switches language mid-conversation).

steps.description: Test each language path end to end and produce the localization plan document.

outputs.name: multilingual-test-results
outputs.desc: Test results for each language: intent accuracy, response correctness, cultural appropriateness

outputs.name: localization-document
outputs.desc: Complete localization document with language coverage, translations, routing, and test results

process: Run the full test suite in each supported language.
Verify intent recognition accuracy per language.
Check response correctness and cultural appropriateness with native speakers.
Compile the localization document.
